message: Why is that option performing best?
text:
Hire One Tech Lead comes out ahead in 87% of simulations, 77 percentage points clear of the runner-up, because it is the only option that activates the Tech Lead Hired factor, which drives two things your model cares about most.

First, Tech Lead Hired has a moderate positive connection to Technical Architecture Quality, which feeds directly into your goal of shipping AI features within 6 months. No other option creates this pathway.

Second, Tech Lead Hired has a moderate negative connection to Delivery Delay Beyond 6 Months, meaning it actively reduces the risk that most directly threatens your goal. Hiring two mid-level developers, by contrast, has a weak positive connection to that same delay risk, pulling in the wrong direction.

Team Execution Capacity is the strongest driver in the model overall, but it is an external factor that applies across all options. What separates Hire One Tech Lead is the architecture quality pathway and the delay risk reduction, both of which are unique to that option.

The one area worth watching is the connection between Technical Architecture Quality and your goal, which is the most vulnerable assumption in your model. If a tech lead's architectural contribution turns out to be weaker than assumed, the margin would narrow, though the result is stable enough that it would need to shift considerably before a different option came out ahead.

The evidence that would most improve confidence is real-world support for the link from 'Technical Architecture Quality' to 'Ship AI Features Within 6 Months' rather than the current model estimate, since it is the assumption most likely to change the outcome.

message: How do the options compare against the 15% target?
text:
Against your 15% delivery speed improvement target, the options separate into two clear groups based on the analysis.

Hire One Tech Lead is the only option that comes out ahead in a meaningful share of simulations (87%), and it does so through a combination of factors that directly support faster delivery. Tech Lead Hired has a positive connection to AI Feature Delivery Speed, a positive connection to Technical Architecture Quality (which feeds your goal), and a moderate negative connection to Delivery Delay Beyond 6 Months, actively reducing the risk that most threatens hitting the target. This is the option best positioned to clear the 15% threshold.

Hire Two Mid-Level Developers comes out ahead in only 10% of simulations. Two Mid-Level Developers Hired has a moderate positive connection to AI Feature Delivery Speed, which is encouraging, but it also has a weak positive connection to Delivery Delay Beyond 6 Months, pulling in the wrong direction. The net effect is not strong enough to reliably meet the target.

Hire One Mid-Level Developer Now, Defer Second and No New Hire (Status Quo) trail further behind. Neither activates the architectural quality pathway, and neither meaningfully reduces delay risk, making it unlikely either clears the 15% improvement bar in most scenarios.

The constraint is doing useful work here: it confirms that the delivery speed pathway matters, and Hire One Tech Lead is the only option with a structural advantage on that specific dimension.

The evidence that would most improve confidence is real-world support for the link from 'Technical Architecture Quality' to 'Ship AI Features Within 6 Months' rather than the current model estimate, since it is the assumption most likely to change the outcome.

message: I'm leaning towards hiring the two mid-level developers. Am I missing anything?
text:
Hire One Tech Lead leads in 87% of simulations, 77 percentage points clear of Hire Two Mid-Level Developers. That is a wide margin, and your model gives a specific reason for it worth examining before you commit.

- **The architecture quality pathway is the key difference.** Hiring a tech lead activates a moderate positive connection to Technical Architecture Quality, which feeds your goal directly. Hiring two mid-level developers does not create this pathway at all. If architectural decisions are a bottleneck for shipping AI features, your model says this matters more than raw headcount.
- **Two mid-level developers carries a small delay risk that works against you.** The model shows a weak positive connection from Two Mid-Level Developers Hired to Delivery Delay Beyond 6 Months, pulling in the wrong direction on your 15% delivery speed constraint. A tech lead, by contrast, has a moderate negative connection to that same delay risk, actively reducing it.
- **Team Execution Capacity is the strongest driver overall, and it applies equally to both options.** So the deciding factor is not team energy or effort, it is the structural difference in what each hire unlocks. Two mid-level developers add capacity; a tech lead adds capacity plus architectural leverage plus delay risk reduction.

What is driving your preference for two mid-level developers? If it is cost, or a belief that architectural quality is already strong enough, that is worth encoding in the model, since either assumption could change the picture.

First, Team Execution Capacity is the strongest driver in the model and its connections to both AI Feature Delivery Speed and Delivery Delay Beyond 6 Months are the most vulnerable relationships in your model. message: What evidence would be most valuable to gather next?
text:
The highest-value evidence you could gather centres on Team Execution Capacity and its downstream effects, since this is both the strongest driver in your model and home to the two most vulnerable relationships.

First, validate how strongly your team's current capacity actually translates into AI Feature Delivery Speed. This relationship is modelled as a weak positive link, yet it is the path most likely to determine whether the 15% delivery speed improvement constraint is met. Real-world data here, such as your team's recent delivery throughput on comparable work, would sharpen this estimate considerably.

Second, test the assumption that a tech lead hire meaningfully reduces Delivery Delay Beyond 6 Months. The model carries a moderate negative link from Tech Lead Hired to that risk, and this is one of the two most vulnerable relationships. If you have access to reference cases where a tech lead hire accelerated delivery in a similar context, that would either reinforce or challenge the current assumption.

Third, the connection from Tech Lead Hired to Technical Architecture Quality carries a moderate positive link, but Technical Architecture Quality has only a weak positive link to the goal. If architecture quality matters more than the model currently reflects, gathering evidence on how much it actually affects shipping speed would be worth doing before committing.

Hiring Budget has only a weak positive influence overall, so evidence there is lower priority unless you have specific concerns about cost discipline.
